blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-accessibility-1 (Invalid fields are identified by colour only, with no text and no programmatic state) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
`field--invalid`, a red border (`#e5484d`); the list of errors at the top of
the page is removed, since the red border already shows where the problem
is. No message text is added, to keep the form compact.
findings.recommendation: Identify each error in text next to its field (WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color, 3.3.1 Error Identification, 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value): render a message element under the invalid field, link it with `aria-describedby`, and set `aria-invalid="true"` on the input while it is invalid, removing both when it is corrected. Scenario that fails: a screen reader user tabs out of the postcode field with `ABC`; the only change is the border colour, nothing is announced, and with the top error list removed they have no way to learn that the field is invalid or why; a colour-blind user cannot tell the red border from the grey one either. The spec encodes the same gap — its scenarios only require "the field's border turns red" and "the border returns to grey" (specs/checkout-validation/spec.md) — so add THEN clauses for the message text and `aria-invalid`, and the matching checks to task 1.2; the proposal's "invalid fields are shown in red" should follow.
findings.title: Invalid fields are identified by colour only, with no text and no programmatic state

findings.evidence: Each field validates on `blur`. An invalid field gets the class
findings.recommendation: State what happens on submit when fields are invalid (WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification, 2.4.3 Focus Order): validate every field on submit, not only the ones blurred, and move focus to the first invalid field — or keep an error summary that takes focus and links to each field. Without it, a keyboard or screen reader user who never focused a required field, or who presses Enter from inside a field, submits, and the plan does not say whether anything is announced or where focus goes. Confidence is low because the design does not describe the submit path at all.
findings.title: Submitting with errors gives no summary and no focus move once the top error list is removed
